questions.question: A trapezium is defined as a quadrilateral with:
options: One pair of opposite sides parallel
Both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of adjacent sides equal
Diagonals that bisect each other

questions.question: A rhombus is best defined as:
options: Any quadrilateral with four equal sides drawn at a slant
A parallelogram with two adjacent sides equal
A rectangle with a right angle
A kite with one pair of parallel sides

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE?
options: Every parallelogram is a rectangle
Every rectangle is a rhombus
Every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus
Every kite is a parallelogram

questions.question: A kite differs from the parallelogram family because it is defined by:
options: Equal diagonals
Four equal angles
One pair of parallel sides
Two pairs of ADJACENT sides equal, with no parallel sides required

subtopics.title: The Parallelogram's Properties, and Where They Come From

questions.question: In the proof that opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD are equal, the diagonal AC is drawn in order to:
options: Bisect the interior angles
Create two triangles in which congruence can be used
Show that the diagonals are equal
Prove the angle sum is 360°

questions.question: The reason for angle BAC = angle DCA is:
options: Vertically opposite angles
Angles opposite equal sides
Alternate angles, AB ∥ DC
Co-interior angles, AD ∥ BC

questions.question: In parallelogram PQRS, angle P = 3x + 10 and angle Q = 2x + 20. Then x equals:
The four angles of that parallelogram are:

subtopics.title: Conditions — Proving a Figure IS a Parallelogram

questions.question: Which of these is a CONDITION sufficient to prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
options: One pair of opposite sides equal
One pair of opposite sides both equal AND parallel
One pair of opposite sides parallel
The diagonals are equal

questions.question: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a:
options: Rhombus
Kite
Rectangle
Trapezium

questions.question: A parallelogram whose diagonals are perpendicular is a:
options: Rectangle
Trapezium
Square, always
Rhombus

questions.question: The difference between a property and a condition is that:
options: A property says what a parallelogram HAS; a condition says what is ENOUGH to conclude a figure is one
A property is proved and a condition is assumed
They mean the same thing in Grade 10
A condition applies only to rectangles

subtopics.title: The Reasoning Chain — Writing a Proof That Scores

questions.question: In the rider on BEDF, the condition aimed at is:
options: One pair of opposite sides equal and parallel
The diagonals bisect each other
Both pairs of opposite angles equal
The diagonals are equal

questions.question: EO = OF is established because:
options: E and F are midpoints of the diagonal
BEDF is given as a parallelogram
Equal lengths AE and CF were subtracted from the equal halves AO and OC
Triangle AEB is congruent to triangle CFD

questions.question: A statement written without a reason beside it:
options: Earns half a mark
Is acceptable if it is obviously true
Only matters in the final line
Earns nothing, however true it is

questions.question: Which belongs in the error museum?
options: Reading a right angle off the sketch because it looks like one
Choosing your target condition before starting
Drawing a diagonal to create triangles
Using standard reason abbreviations

subtopics.title: The Family Where Every Child Inherits

questions.question: In the family picture, the parallelogram's one new rule is:
options: Four equal sides
Square corners
Both pairs of opposite sides run parallel
Equal diagonals

questions.question: The blazer-and-badge uniform picture teaches that:
options: Every shape needs a proof
Inheritance runs downward only — a badge proves membership, but the blazer does not prove prefecthood
Rectangles and rhombuses are unrelated
A square has no parent shape

questions.question: The rhombus adds which single thing to the parallelogram?
options: Equal side lengths — all four the same
Square corners
Parallel sides
Equal diagonals

questions.question: Cutting a parallelogram corner to corner gives:
options: Two triangles of different sizes
Two identical triangles, one turned around
Two kites
Four small parallelograms

questions.question: The 'slanting road crossing two parallel streets' pictures which fact?
options: The diagonals bisect each other
The angle sum is 360°
The angles the diagonal makes at the two parallel sides are equal
All four sides are equal

questions.question: Two corners next to each other in a parallelogram add to:
Neighbouring corners of 3x + 10 and 2x + 20 give the four angles:

subtopics.title: A Proof Is a Chain of Receipts

questions.question: The 'receipt' in the analogy stands for:
options: The final conclusion
The reason written beside each statement
The diagram
The given information only

questions.question: Why may you not use a parallelogram's properties on a figure straight away?
options: Because properties only apply to rectangles
Because the properties have not been proved yet
Because you cannot use the receipt for something you have not yet shown you own — the figure must first be proved a parallelogram
Because a proof must always begin with congruence

questions.question: In the BEDF question, the first thing to decide is:
options: How many marks it carries
Whether the figure is a rhombus
Which triangles are congruent
What you are aiming at — which condition you will prove

questions.question: Which of the three closing habits was given?
options: Never trust the picture — a sketch that looks like a right angle is not one until something proves it
Measure the sketch carefully with a protractor
Write only the statements, since reasons are optional
Start from the conclusion and work backwards without stating it
